question: If the equation \((x-2)^2=k-3\) in \(x\) has two distinct real roots, what is the range of \(k\)?
solution: \((x-2)^2\) is nonnegative. For two distinct real roots, \(k-3>0\) is required, so \(k>3\). When \(k=3\), there is only one root; when \(k<3\), there are no real roots.
